null_rate is 0.0 with distinct_count 16 holding fully spelled carrier names (e.g. 'Delta Air Lines Inc.', 'JetBlue Airways'); renamed from the ambiguous 'name' to carrier_name per the operator's instruction to spell out abbreviated column names and disambiguate.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.
carrier_code has distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so it uniquely identifies each row and is declared the sole grain key.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning (a run-level timestamp and an empty JSON object), so all three are dropped.
Per operator context, code columns are named with a _code suffix, so bronze 'carrier' (16 distinct two-letter values, null_rate 0.0) becomes carrier_code.
Per operator context to spell out abbreviated names and avoid ambiguity, bronze 'name' (16 distinct full carrier names, null_rate 0.0) becomes carrier_name.

purpose: This table is the cleaned carrier reference lookup for the nycflights13-derived NYC airlines dataset, mapping each two-letter carrier code to its full legal airline name, for use as a dimension table joined against flight fact tables on carrier_code.
usage: Join downstream flight or fare tables to this table on carrier_code to resolve the full carrier_name for reporting; the table is small (16 rows), fully populated, and requires no null handling or deduplication by consumers.
limitations: The source profile shows zero nulls and zero duplicate rows across all five bronze columns, so no cleanup ambiguities remain; the three Airbyte capture-metadata columns were dropped entirely and carry no business value, and the table captures only the 2013 NYC-origin carrier roster documented by the nycflights13 package, not a live or comprehensive BTS carrier list.
